name: AngelList / Wellfound

sources.title: angel.co now serves Wellfound — 'AI recruiting platform for startups'; post jobs free; company signup at wellfound.com/onboarding/recruit

requirements: angel.co resolves to Wellfound (the former AngelList Talent product) — the original AngelList startup-profile directory is now the Wellfound recruiting platform
Free tier: 'Unlimited jobs, unlimited applicants, and a built-in ATS are $0 forever' — creating a company profile and posting jobs is free
Paid options: promoting a job for visibility, Wellfound Reach (AI sourcing), and Autopilot (managed recruiting)
Company signup path: wellfound.com/onboarding/recruit (or 'Sign up' → 'I'm looking to hire')
The value for a SaaS launch is a public startup profile on wellfound.com — the old angel.co/company/<name> profile convention is gone
preparation: Company details for the Wellfound profile: name, logo, description, website, size, funding status
At least one job posting to activate the recruiting side (optional but the platform's core loop)
workflow: Open angel.co (resolves to Wellfound) or wellfound.com directly
Sign up and choose 'I'm looking to hire' → onboarding/recruit
Create the company profile and optionally post a free job
The public company page appears at wellfound.com/company/<name>
Optionally upgrade for promoted jobs, Reach AI sourcing, or Autopilot recruiting
watchFor: The catalog flag 'Domain redirects elsewhere' is real — angel.co is now entirely Wellfound-branded; fundraising/AngelList VC functions moved to angel.co/venture under a different product surface
This is a recruiting marketplace — the startup profile is a byproduct of hiring, not a launch listing; profiles without jobs are thin
Wellfound profiles historically ranked well in search ('AngelList <startup>'), which is the SEO value here
countsAsLive: A public company profile exists at wellfound.com/company/<name> with jobs/details visible
unknowns: Whether a company profile can be created without posting a job
What happened to legacy angel.co profile pages — redirect vs removal
